launch-email.notes: K is structurally sound but almost entirely bracketed placeholders, so it delivers little concrete value or persuasive copy. L and M are both specific, scannable and built around one primary CTA with features clearly marked as assumptions; L has punchier subject options while M adds a useful warning not to promise unshipped features, and both slightly dilute the single CTA with a P.S. and add some extra commentary.

yoga-landing.notes: K is the most complete and polished: a working accessible mobile menu, ARIA day tabs, form validation, a distinctive earthy design and full responsive breakpoints, though it invents realistic-looking specifics (a real Portland street address, 600+ reviews) and hides content behind JS reveal and JS-rendered schedule. L is also polished, with dark mode, a semantic table schedule and good accessibility, but it simply hides nav links on mobile and uses invented stats and testimonials; M is clean and highly accessible but visually generic with grey placeholder boxes, has no nav at all below 1100px, and leaks references to unseen instructions ('eleven sections in the requested order', 'fallback palette').

summary.notes: M is faithful, leads with the decision, adds correct derived context (310K is about 85% of growth, about 10% cost drop) and groups risks well, with one small slip in saying HR 'will pilot' when the source only says HR proposes it. K is accurate and complete but files the Pune delay under 'Decision needed'; L is accurate and concise but leaves out the Chennai recovery and the Bengaluru growth driver, which execs would want.
